content: Progressive disseminated histoplasmosis (PDH) is a severe fungal infection that commonly affects individuals living with HIV. The optimal treatment approach for this condition remains uncertain. For induction therapy, one randomized controlled trial (RCT) compared liposomal amphotericin B to deoxycholate amphotericin B. The results suggest that liposomal amphotericin B may lead to higher clinical success rates compared to deoxycholate amphotericin B (risk ratio [RR] 1.46, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.01 to 2.11; low-certainty evidence). Additionally, liposomal amphotericin B was associated with significantly lower rates of nephrotoxicity compared to deoxycholate amphotericin B (RR 0.25, 95% CI 0.09 to 0.67; high-certainty evidence). However, there is very low-certainty evidence available to compare amphotericin B formulations with azoles for induction therapy. Regarding maintenance therapy, no eligible studies were identified that directly compared shorter durations of oral antifungal treatment (less than 12 months) to the standard 12 months or longer. Fluconazole was found to perform poorly in comparison to other azoles for both induction and maintenance therapy. For antiretroviral therapy (ART) initiation, one study reported that one out of seven participants in the early ART initiation group died, while none of the three participants in the delayed ART initiation group died. However, the evidence in this area is extremely limited. In conclusion, liposomal amphotericin B appears to be a superior option compared to deoxycholate amphotericin B for the treatment of PDH in individuals with HIV, particularly due to its lower nephrotoxicity and potentially higher clinical success rates. Fluconazole is less effective compared to other azoles. There is insufficient or very low-certainty evidence to guide decisions regarding other induction therapies, maintenance therapy durations, or the timing of ART initiation. Further prospective comparative trials are urgently needed to provide clearer guidance for clinical decision-making in the management of PDH.
